judge.reasoning: The system answer explicitly states that MultiHead is computed by concatenating the heads, satisfying the reference fact 'Concat'.

rows.answer:
MultiHead(Q, K, V) is computed by concatenating multiple attention heads and then projecting the result with a parameter matrix $W^O$:

$$\text{MultiHead}(Q, K, V) = \text{Concat}(\text{head}_1, ..., \text{head}_h)W^O$$
$$\text{where } \text{head}_i = \text{Attention}(QW_i^Q, KW_i^K, VW_i^V)$$

where the projections are parameter matrices:
- $W_i^Q \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}$
- $W_i^K \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}$
- $W_i^V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_v}$
- $W^O \in \mathbb{R}^{h d_v \times d_{\text{model}}}$

rows.answer:
The late-interaction operator $\text{LI}(q, d)$ is computed as the sum over all query vectors $\mathbf{E}_q^{(i)}$ of their maximum dot product with each of the $N_d$ document embedding vectors $\mathbf{E}_d^{(j)}$. Formally, it is expressed as:

$$\text{LI}(q, d) = \sum_{i \in [1, N_q]} \max_{j \in [1, N_d]} \langle \mathbf{E}_q^{(i)} | \mathbf{E}_d^{(j)} \rangle$$
